why: The finding picks out the planted late-delivery spikes. Order jobs with a weld operation shipped on time 0.8016 of the time in 2016 and 0.851 in 2021, against 0.9846-0.9978 in other years; jobs without weld were 0.9154 in 2016 and 0.7898 in 2021 (t442). It also correctly says 2016 was a delay inside the plant that is not explained by material. But it never reaches the planted cause: due dates set from a standard lead time with no check on the load at the bottleneck work centres. It says it could not tell which work centre held jobs, and it puts about 0.39 of the 2021 excess on vendor lead times. Truth hours by work centre are completion-dated and do not by themselves settle the bottleneck question (weld 50,379 h in 2016 and 47,166 h in 2021, against 42,488-49,672 h in other years, t443). So this is the right effect with the mechanism missing.
